title: Lakewood
name: Lakewood
metaDescription: Lakewood 1031 exchange guidance for Belmar mixed-use retail, Federal Center-area office, and West Colfax corridor property west of Denver.

sections.html: Lakewood sits directly west of Denver, and it's one of the older, more built-out suburbs in the metro. The commercial stock runs from a redeveloped mall-turned-town-center down to older strip retail along West Colfax, and that range is what makes this submarket worth understanding property by property rather than by a single average.

sections.heading: Belmar Replaced a Dead Mall
sections.html:
Belmar sits on the old Villa Italia mall site, which closed and got torn down in the early 2000s. What replaced it is a mixed-use town center, street grid, ground-floor retail, apartments and offices above, public plazas, and it's the clearest example in this metro of what an enclosed mall redevelopment can look like when it works. Colorado Mills, an outlet-format mall a few miles away, is a different asset class entirely and shouldn't be comped against Belmar even though both sit inside Lakewood.

The Green Mountain neighborhood on Lakewood's west side is worth flagging separately, it's almost entirely residential, built up through the 1970s and 1980s, with little standalone commercial inventory of its own. Investors looking at that part of the city are generally looking at small neighborhood-serving retail on the fringe rather than any larger commercial parcel.

The Union Boulevard corridor, running north-south through central Lakewood, carries a mix of mid-rise office and medical buildings that predate both Belmar and the Federal Center's more recent growth. This stock tends to trade at a discount to newer Belmar-area product, and a buyer willing to take on deferred maintenance can find a meaningfully lower entry basis here than on the redeveloped side of the city.

sections.heading: Property Types Actually Available Here
sections.html:
What comes up for sale in Lakewood right now:

  • mixed-use retail and office buildings in and around Belmar
  • outlet and big-box retail near Colorado Mills
  • office and flex space near the Denver Federal Center
  • older strip retail and light industrial along West Colfax Avenue

sections.heading: The Federal Center Is a Different Kind of Anchor
sections.html: The Denver Federal Center is a large federal government campus on Lakewood's east side, and it employs thousands of workers across dozens of agencies. Office and flex space near it benefits from that steady federal workforce in a way that has nothing to do with retail traffic or apartment demand elsewhere in the city. It's a stable tenant base, but government-adjacent leasing moves on its own slower timeline, and a buyer should factor that into any renewal assumption.

sections.heading: West Colfax Is Still Working Through It
sections.html:
West Colfax Avenue carries some of the oldest strip retail in the metro, built for a driving public in the 1950s and 1960s, and parts of it have struggled with vacancy and deferred maintenance for years. Redevelopment has picked up in patches, but a buyer looking at a West Colfax parcel needs a real vacancy history on the building itself, separate from the corridor's redevelopment narrative, before underwriting a rent bump.

Sixth Avenue, the freeway running along Lakewood's northern edge, carries its own strip of flex and light industrial buildings that lease on visibility and easy freeway access rather than neighborhood foot traffic. That corridor comps more sensibly against similar freeway-adjacent flex space elsewhere in the metro than against anything on West Colfax a mile south.

sections.heading: Positioning a Lakewood Identification
sections.html: Belmar retail tends to be the strongest single Lakewood asset on an identification list given its mixed-use design and steady foot traffic. Buyers often pair it with a Federal Center-area office building for tenant diversification, or with a Golden or Highlands Ranch property if they want geographic spread across the west and south sides of the Denver metro. A qualified intermediary should confirm parking easement and reciprocal access agreements on any Belmar-area building before closing, since much of the district shares structured parking across multiple ownership parcels. That same reciprocal easement review applies to any Colorado Mills outparcel too, given how outlet-format centers typically structure shared drive aisles and common-area maintenance across separately owned pads. A rent roll comparison across Lakewood's four property types, Belmar, Colorado Mills, Federal Center office, and West Colfax strip retail, should never be blended into one average, since each responds to a different tenant base and a different set of demand drivers. Note the exact corridor by name on any identification paperwork rather than the city alone, since that specificity matters if a lender or tax advisor needs to reconstruct the deal's reasoning later.

faqs.q: Is Belmar retail a solid 1031 replacement property?
faqs.a: It's generally the strongest single asset class in Lakewood, given its mixed-use design and consistent foot traffic since the Villa Italia mall redevelopment. Confirm individual tenant lease terms rather than assuming the whole district performs uniformly.

faqs.q: Should Colorado Mills be comped against Belmar?
faqs.a: No. They're different formats, an outlet mall versus a mixed-use town center, even though both sit inside Lakewood. Comp each against its own asset class.

faqs.q: How stable is office space near the Denver Federal Center?
faqs.a: Reasonably stable given the federal workforce base, but government-adjacent leasing and renewal timelines move slower than private-sector office, so build that into any underwriting timeline.

faqs.q: Is West Colfax retail a good value-add opportunity?
faqs.a: Some parcels are, but get the actual building's vacancy and maintenance history rather than relying on the corridor's broader redevelopment story to justify a rent increase.

faqs.q: What does a Lakewood identification typically get paired with?
faqs.a: A Federal Center office asset for tenant diversification, or a Golden or Highlands Ranch property for geographic spread across the west and south sides of the metro.
